spec: LORE_DISCOVERY v0.1, slice 1 (design repo, private): an optional weekday lesson with Lizzy, a homework row to the plaza plaque and back, Archivist Mo's shelf as a talk menu, three chatter lines and Journal notes. Decisions D2280-D2296.

lz_war: A new word is up on the chalkboard: THE GREAT WAR. Pip and Tilly are already arguing about it.
Today: the Great War. It was a long time ago. We skip the fighting part in this room.
Two loud answers, like always. The Keepers' books say the lanterns stayed lit on every road.
My mom says the hard years are when partnership started. Glimmerwell made a poster about it.
The book gives them one line, Pip. Then the page stops. Picking Day started right after.
lz_war_home: Lizzy is marking at her desk. The card on top says THE GREAT WAR.
You missed my war lesson! Fine. Kitchen-table version. Buddy, you're the class.
The Keepers' books say the lanterns stayed lit. Glimmerwell's poster says partnership started.
The book gives Walklings one line. Then the page stops, and Picking Day starts. I checked. Twice.
lz_war_end: Good. Ask the old ones. Della at the Lantern House knows who they are.
Good. Archivist Mo keeps the old books at the Keeper House. Wash your hands first.
Homework. Read the plaque in the plaza, then tell me who the next holder is. No, Buddy doesn't count.
lz_war_plaque: A stone Keeper holds a lantern over the water. The plaque reads: KEEP THE LIGHT FOR THE NEXT HOLDER.
That's Lizzy's homework. She'll want the answer in your own words.
lz_war_back: Homework! So. Who's the next holder?
You tell her: whoever comes after you.
Right. So you keep the light, and you write things down for them. That's the whole job.
And keep asking the old ones. They forget what nobody asks them.
And keep reading. A missing page is a clue too.
Lizzy presses a gold star sticker onto {pet}. It stays on for almost a minute.
mo_shelf_menu: The Arbiter, over in their house, has been emitting for ages.
The books fear a child born already listening. We have not seen one.
The emission has no name. The oldest page leaves that space empty.
The hum woke all five. My books call them the Answerers. The page on what they answer stays blank.
The war shelf is short. The pages that are not on it are the interesting part.
In the war, one Hall Stone was carried whole to the capital. It is still in chains. My page on why is blank.
One old book says someone nearly gathered eight Seals. It does not say who. I do not guess.

objPatch._note: game.js applyObjPatch, after every overlay. Lizzy keys sit after every built key and before else; Mo keeps his lines (the menu follows his plain line through `after`, so a later key placed before standing.keepers>=1 keeps its order). A missing id is skipped.

journalNotes.line: Lizzy's war lesson: the book gives Walklings one line, then the page stops. Picking Day came after.
Mo's old books: the Arbiter has been emitting for ages. Its emission has no name.
Mo's old books: five that answer a hum, the Answerers. What they answer is a blank page.
Mo's war shelf: one Hall Stone sits in chains in the capital. His page on why is blank.
